title: A Phone Call About Forgiving a Business Partner
script: Farah: [tense] Bagas, I need to talk to you about the money you were supposed to invest in our shop last month. It still hasn't arrived.
Bagas: [nervous] I know, Farah, and I'm sorry. Things happened that I didn't expect, and I should have called you sooner to explain everything.
Farah: [frustrated] Because of that delay, I had to borrow money from my brother just to pay our supplier on time.
Bagas: [ashamed] I feel terrible hearing that. I promised you that money would come through, and instead I put you in a difficult position.
Farah: [curious] What actually happened, Bagas? You've always been reliable before this, so I'm confused about what changed.
Bagas: [honestly] My father got sick suddenly, and the hospital bills used almost everything I had saved for the shop this year.
Farah: [softening] Why didn't you just tell me that immediately, instead of staying quiet and letting me wonder what was going on?
Bagas: [regretfully] I was embarrassed, honestly. I didn't want you to think I couldn't handle both my family and our business at the same time.
Farah: [gently] I would have understood completely if you had just explained it. Silence was what actually hurt more than the missing money did.
Bagas: [quietly] You're right. I should have trusted you with the truth instead of avoiding your calls for almost two weeks.
Farah: [reflective] Family comes before business, Bagas. If your father was sick, that money was exactly where it needed to be.
Bagas: [relieved] Thank you for saying that. I was afraid you would end our partnership over this.
Farah: [warmly] I was hurt, but I'm not going to throw away three years of trust because of one difficult month.
Bagas: [determined] I'll send what I can by next week, and the rest once my father recovers and I'm working again properly.
Farah: [gently] Take the time you need. Just promise you'll talk to me next time, instead of disappearing when things get hard.
Bagas: [sincerely] I promise. And thank you for forgiving me, even though I honestly didn't handle this well at all.
Farah: [warmly] Everyone struggles sometimes, Bagas. What matters now is that we keep building this shop together, honestly, from here forward.

quiz.question: Why does Farah call Bagas at the start?
options: To end their friendship
Because the money he promised to invest never arrived
To ask him to work longer hours
To plan a trip
quiz.explanation: Farah calls because the money Bagas was supposed to invest in their shop last month still hasn't arrived.

quiz.question: What actually happened to Bagas's money?
options: He lost it gambling
His father got sick, and hospital bills used his savings
He spent it on a vacation
He gave it to another business
quiz.explanation: Bagas's father got sick suddenly, and the hospital bills used almost everything he had saved.

quiz.question: Why didn't Bagas tell Farah sooner?
options: He forgot
He was embarrassed and didn't want her to think he couldn't handle everything
He was too busy to call
He didn't have her number
quiz.explanation: Bagas admits he was embarrassed and didn't want Farah to think he couldn't handle his family and the business.

quiz.question: What does Farah say hurt her more than the missing money?
options: The amount of money itself
Bagas's silence and avoiding her calls
Losing the shop
Borrowing from her brother
quiz.explanation: Farah says silence was what actually hurt more than the missing money.

quiz.question: What does Farah decide about their partnership?
options: She ends it immediately
She forgives him and wants to keep building the shop together
She demands all the money at once
She asks someone else to be her partner
quiz.explanation: Farah decides not to throw away three years of trust and wants to keep building the shop together.
